grand_strategy.reading: Under President Hilda Heine, the Marshall Islands runs its foreign policy inside a treaty it cannot leave cheaply: the Compact pays for the state and carries its defence, and the 2023 extension bought twenty years, not a settlement of the nuclear grievance. Inside that frame it has three instruments it actually uses: the Taipei tie, one of three Pacific recognitions left; a flag registry, second largest in the world as of 2017, whose foreign-owned ships the United States said it would not defend at sea; and the visa-free right to live and work in America, which makes emigration a lever. The sea is the one constraint no treaty can renegotiate: the country averages seven feet above sea level, and a US$1 billion radar site at Kwajalein is on the list of what rising seas could threaten.

stances.note: Treaty ally: the Compact of Free Association carries the money and the defence (DOI, read in full; the Ninth Circuit quotes the Compact). The bond under the posture is grievance: the nuclear testing at Bikini, and a Nuclear Claims Tribunal award of about US$2 billion that was never paid (Guardian, 2014), with the LA Times reading the relation as a betrayal (2019). Grade follows structure, so the treaty sets the posture and the grievance sits as the bond: the pair reads as a Byzantine alliance, which the build will show as a fault. Trend stable: the Compact was extended for twenty years in 2023 (Reuters via Japan Times, not opened), while the Wake Island claim stays on the books.

stances_toward.note: Rival by recognition, and the contest runs through the Pacific forum more than through Majuro. Relations with Beijing are listed as suspended (DOI list, mirrored below) while the Marshall Islands keeps Taipei. In August 2026 the Foreign Ministry told the Pacific Islands Forum secretary to keep to the one-China principle after he said Taipei would attend the forum in 2026: the pressure reaches Majuro as a forum member, not as a bilateral act. Not adversary: Beijing wants the recognition, not the state. Stable: nothing read shows a new act toward the Marshall Islands since 2018. Bond none. Confidence C: the MFA page is tier 1 for the relation; the rival reading is ours, and no Marshallese or PRC statement on the pair has been read.
